items.title: Over 23,000 vehicles denied entry into Delhi in two days over pollution norms
items.summary: To control pollution in Delhi, the government has tightened restrictions on vehicles coming in from outside the city. Buses and other vehicles entering Delhi must now meet BS-VI emission standards. To enforce this, police and transport department teams have been stationed at various border checkpoints to inspect incoming vehicles. Those that do not meet BS-VI standards are being stopped at the borders, and in some cases they are also being fined (challaned) or impounded. Newslaundry visited the DND Flyway, Kalindi Kunj, and Chilla Gaon borders to assess the situation. At all three checkpoints, police and transport department teams were present, inspecting vehicles entering the city. At Kalindi Kunj, police inspected about 500 vehicles between morning and evening. Of these, 50 were turned back, while 20 were fined for violating pollution norms. Watch this report. Complaining about the media is easy. Why not do something to make it better? items.title: Ill while in jail but now wants to go abroad for job? Kerala High Court on Tomin Thachankery plea
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Monday questioned the apparent contradiction in a plea made by corruption-accused former Kerala Director General of Police (DGP) Tomin J Thachankary seeking permission to travel abroad for work, despite having earlier claimed that he suffered from various medical ailments while he faced the prospect of remaining in jail. Thachankary's latest plea seeks a relaxation of conditions imposed by the High Court in October, when it suspended a four-year prison sentence imposed in him by a trial court in a disproportionate assets case. Justice A Badharudeen today recounted that Thachankary had earlier claimed he suffered from various health conditions when he urged the trial court to take a lenient approach in his sentencing. "While in jail, he says he has so many illnesses. Now he is asking permission to go abroad to do a job. Why such contradictions?" remarked Justice Badharudeen. items.title: Courts reviewing arbitral award on merits defeats purposes of arbitration: Chief Justice Vibhu Bahkru
items.summary: Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru on Saturday said that allowing courts to undertake a full merit-based review of arbitral awards would defeat the fundamental purpose of arbitration, which was intended to provide parties with a final adjudication of disputes outside the traditional court system. Speaking at a conference on Ethics and Evidence in Arbitration in Bengaluru, Justice Bakhru acknowledged concerns over the quality of arbitral awards but cautioned against expanding judicial scrutiny. " But if you have a full merits review then automatically the private arbitration is over ," Justice Bakhru said. The conference was jointly hosted by the London Court of International Arbitration (LCIA), ArbitralWomen and the Arbitration and Conciliation Centre Bengaluru at the Karnataka Judicial Academy. Justice Bakhru made the observation during a fireside conversation with Senior Advocate Shashank Garg , a Court Member of the LCIA, on the hits and misses of India's arbitration landscape.
